categories.label: Chambers
categories.blurb: Two atria receive blood; two ventricles eject it. Wall thickness follows the pressure each chamber must generate.

categories.label: Valves
categories.blurb: Four valves enforce one-way flow. They open and close passively, driven entirely by pressure differences across them.

categories.label: Septa
categories.blurb: The interatrial and interventricular septa separate the right and left circulations.

categories.label: Coronary Circulation
categories.blurb: The heart's own blood supply — arteries that fill mainly in diastole, and veins that return to the right atrium.

categories.label: Conduction System
categories.blurb: Specialised myocardium that generates and distributes the electrical impulse, setting rate and coordinating contraction.

categories.label: Great Vessels
categories.blurb: The large arteries and veins entering and leaving the heart, linking the pulmonary and systemic circuits.

categories.label: Major Arteries
categories.blurb: The systemic arterial tree: distribution, resistance and the cushioning of pulsatile flow.

categories.label: Major Veins
categories.blurb: The systemic venous system: the body's capacitance reservoir and the route back to the right heart.
